Palette, lookup-table, kernel geometry, sample positions, transition timing, and text-slot extents are named in aligned TU-private domains. The two implementation-only headers and obsolete semantic ratchet were removed; remaining zeros/ones are coordinates, channel bounds, loop termination, or boolean resource translation. Allocation/free operands preserve retail source-line evidence. Private placement improves the retail code shape while preserving relocation targets.
The implementation contains no policy literals; constructor zeros are empty-widget initialization and all other numerics are address/size annotations.

Manager results, dispatch states, priority, and capacity are private named constants; dialog storage derives from sizeof(executive), and executable selection uses the shared game/editor selectors. Non-debug section bytes and ordered relocations are unchanged.

TU-private orientation, result, color-table, and draw-extent enums are aligned and use prefix-free value names. Remaining zeros/ones are clipping origins, inclusive-bound adjustments, booleans, or low-level draw flags; allocation/free operands 18 and 0x1a preserve retail source-line evidence. Resource lifecycle is named and non-debug sections/relocations remain exact.

Private resource-name capacity, color mask, center shift, and bottom padding are enums; dispatch results use the shared ABI domain. Remaining zeros/ones are initialization, booleans, frame origins, or resource lookup flags.

Cursor sizes, offsets, and hotspot pairs remain retail data payloads, while allocation/assert operands preserve source-location evidence. Reference lifecycle and palette extents are named; allocation/free operands 8, 13, and 21 preserve retail source-line evidence, while zero is the empty resource id. Pointer state uses NULL.
